speaker: Doctor
text: Let's clarify your symptoms: when did the shooting ear pain start relative to your tympanoplasty surgery, and does pressing on the tragus or pulling your earlobe reproduce the pain? Also, how would you describe the difficulty wearing earrings—is it due to pain, swelling, or simply not being able to insert them?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details; the shooting pain while eating suggests possible involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve or Eustachian tube dysfunction, while the earring discomfort could indicate granulation tissue or a fibrous scar band. Have you noticed any drainage, dizziness, or a sensation of fullness in the right ear since the surgery?

REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy to inspect the tympanic membrane and ear canal for granulation tissue or retraction pockets.
REQUEST IMAGES: Otoscopic_photo_right_ear.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Otoscopy of the right ear reveals a healthy tympanic membrane with no evidence of granulation tissue, retraction pockets, or active drainage. The ear canal is clear. The patient reports no sensation of fullness or dizziness.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia with possible granulation tissue at the tympanoplasty site.
